editor_interpretation: truncations of commodity/measure words (κοτύ(λην) πυ(ρῶν); χοίν(ικες); μιμα(ικύλων); Μαργα(ρίτες)); numerals (ϛο'=76; δ'; π'=80 Hasmonaean era?); personal names in genitive ([Ἀ]πφου/[Σα]πφου; [Ῥο]ύφου); 1098: ΗΛ and ΚΟ 'may represent a personal name (possibly name+patronymic or name+ethnic) referring to the importer', ΗΠ = 88 (year 56/55 BCE) or ἡδύποτος (LDS)
relevance: closest functional parallel in the core window: short Greek letter groups labelling containers in Herodian Jerusalem, read as abbreviated contents/measures/dates/names. None equals a target group.

source: CIIP I.1 nos. 84(b) ΚΝΙΦ; 112 ΙΦΚΧ; 113 ΧΨ/ΑΒ; 509 ΘΗ; 606 ΕΔΧΨ?; 227 ΓΑ; 263 ΗΔ
editor_interpretation: JJP (Price): 'initials' (Tzaferis, Rahmani) rejected: 'difficult to know what the initials would stand for in the conventional nomenclature of the period, when family names were rare' (112); 'this was not the practice in ossuary inscriptions' (509); preferred: alphabet-adjacent pairs as atbash/albam/aḥas cryptic or apotropaic letters (Bij de Vaate); 84(b) possibly letter-shift +2 encoding of שלום; 263 ΗΔ = abridged Ἡδήα (authenticity doubted)
relevance: these are the Rahmani CJO 289/319/322/582 groups cited by wave 1 as 'initials': CIIP editors reject the initials reading. Post hoc check: the CIIP pairs are alphabet-adjacent (ΙΚ, ΦΧ, ΑΒ, ΧΨ, ΘΗ, ΕΔ); none of the seven Copper Scroll groups contains an adjacent-letter pair (0/7), so the scroll groups do not follow this cryptic-pair pattern.

letters: ΓΟΡΑΣ, ΚΑΣΙΑΣ, ΑΠΟΛΛ, ΑΠΟΛ, ΑΠ, Α+, ΑΡ/ΡΑ monogram, ΗΖ/ΖΗ, [--]ΟΛΛΑ, ΛΑ, ΜΑ/ΛΛΑ, ΠΑ, ΔΙΣ, ΑΘ, ΕΟ, Θ̣Ε̣, single Α
editor_interpretation: 'most probably owners' marks' - names written in full or cut to 1-5 letters (AE, after Warner Slane)
relevance: a regional system of abbreviated personal names on vessels; supplies ΔΙΣ (partial ΔΙ) and an uncertain ΘΕ; no ΚΕΝ/ΧΑΓ/ΗΝ/ΤΡ/ΣΚ

letters: Χ(126 stones), Γ, Σ, Ο, ΙΟ/ΟΙ, Ο, Α, Η, ΤΟ, Τ, Δ, Ψ, Ε/Ψ, ΔΙ(4), Π, Λ, Ζ?
editor_interpretation: counting/accounting marks for workmen or workgroups, cut in the quarry (WE)
relevance: shows that 1-2-letter Greek marks identifying responsible work-units existed in the Decapolis; only ΔΙ coincides

editor_interpretation: Δι(ονυσίου) (sc. ἀμφόδου), sector reserved for a city quarter; parallel Φυλ(ῆς) Διονυσιάδος at Neapolis; ed. pr. numeral 14 rejected
relevance: ΔΙ as an abbreviated name label (B)
ΤΡ(Υ) used to abbreviate the name Tryphon (non-Jewish king); supports 'ΤΡ = Tryphon'-type readings only as a format, not as evidence for any Copper Scroll person

source: Puech 2006 vol. I pp. 174-175 n. 46; Puech 2015 pp. 12-13 n. 46 (citing Porath-Yannai-Kasher, 'Atiqot 37, 1999, 1-78 [Heb.], 167*-171*)
letters: ΑΓΡΙΠΠΑΣ ΑΓΡΙΠ ΑΓΡ ΑΓ Α; ΒΕΡΕΝΙΚΗ ΒΕΡΕΝ ΒΕΡΝ ΒΕΡ ΒΕ Β; ΖΩΗΛΟΥΣ ΖΩΗ ΖΩ; ΘΝΗ(Σ); ΜΑΡΙΑΜΗ ΜΑΡΙΑ ΜΑΡΙ ΜΑΡ; ΜΝΑΣ(εας)/Μ(α)ΝΑΣ(σης); ΠΑΤΡ(ος); ΡΕΒ(εκα)
editor_interpretation: Puech: family members could read and complete the partly engraved names; 'confirmation' of the anthroponym interpretation
relevance: SECONDARY (not checked against 'Atiqot 37 or CIIP II, neither available; IIP has only one Jatt record, with full names). Strongest regional parallel for the abbreviated-name format (1 c. CE, Jewish family tomb - Ilan lists Jatt bearers, e.g. Tehinah no. 7 Θνη[ς]). Attests 0 of the 7 target groups, and every abbreviation sits in the same tomb as the full names.

item: Abbreviated personal names in Jewish-related Greek papyri (Egypt)
source: CPJ V no. 644 (P.NYU II 52), CPJ vol. V text pp. 50-52; CPJ IV no. 574 (P.Polit.Iud. 18), vol. IV pp. 128-129
letters: Τρ( ) (heading l.1 and l.16 of a grain daybook of mostly Jewish names with amounts); θ̣ε̣( ) ηρα( ) in a registration docket
editor_interpretation: 644: list of persons (names often abbreviated: Σαμβα( ), Δημοκ( ), Κλα( )) + place + grain amounts; 574: 'perhaps Ἡρα(κλέους πόλει)... or Θε(όμνηστος) Ἡρα(κλείδου)' (editors uncertain)
relevance: comparanda outside the window: an account format of [abbreviated name] + [place] + [amount], with Τρ( ) and possibly Θε( ) as name abbreviations. CPJ I-III text layers are OCR junk for Greek and were not searchable.
